Great rivalries, by first meeting.Harvard vs Yale football: Known simply as 'The Game', their 1968 meeting ended 29-29 after Harvard scored 16 points in the last 42 seconds, a score famed in the Ivy League.
Great rivalries, by first meeting.Calcutta Cup: The trophy was made from melted silver rupees, the leftover funds of a Calcutta rugby club that had disbanded.
Great rivalries, by first meeting.The Ashes: After England's defeat at The Oval, a mock obituary said English cricket had died and 'the ashes' would go to Australia. A tiny urn now symbolizes it.
Great rivalries, by first meeting.Old Firm derby: Celtic beat Rangers 5-2 in their first meeting. The fierce Glasgow derby blends football with religion and politics.
Great rivalries, by first meeting.Army vs Navy football: Cadets and midshipmen march on to the field, and US presidents often attend, traditionally switching sides at halftime.
Great rivalries, by first meeting.Davis Cup: American Dwight Davis, a player himself, bought the trophy, and the first match in 1900 in Boston was won by the US over the British Isles.
Great rivalries, by first meeting.El Clasico: The first meeting came in a 1902 cup, which Barcelona won 3-1. Today the match is among the world's most-watched club games.
Great rivalries, by first meeting.Bledisloe Cup: The trophy was donated by a New Zealand governor-general, Lord Bledisloe, and is contested between the All Blacks and Wallabies.
Great rivalries, by first meeting.Solheim Cup: Named for Karsten Solheim, the founder of Ping golf clubs, who helped create the women's team contest.
Great rivalries, by first meeting.Presidents Cup: This biennial match pits the US against a team of non-European players. In 2003 it ended in a tie, with a playoff decided in near darkness.

Diamond clarity grades.FL: No inclusions or blemishes are visible even at 10x magnification, and such stones are extremely rare.
Diamond clarity grades.IF: There are no internal flaws under 10x magnification, though tiny surface blemishes may remain.
Diamond clarity grades.VVS1: The flaws are so tiny that even trained graders struggle to find them under 10x magnification.
Diamond clarity grades.VVS2: A hair easier to spot than VVS1, its flaws are still very hard to find even under a jeweler's loupe.
Diamond clarity grades.VS1: Minor inclusions can be found under 10x with some effort, but the naked eye sees a clean stone.
Diamond clarity grades.VS2: Its small inclusions are visible under a loupe but not to the eye, which is why this grade is a popular value choice.
Diamond clarity grades.SI1: Inclusions are easy to see at 10x, yet most of these stones still look clean to the naked eye.
Diamond clarity grades.SI2: Flaws may be visible to the unaided eye in some stones, especially when viewed from the top.
Diamond clarity grades.I1: Inclusions are visible without magnification and may slightly cloud the stone's sparkle.
Diamond clarity grades.I2: The flaws are obvious and can dull brilliance or even weaken the stone; the GIA scale goes one step further to I3.

Track gauge: the distance between the ra.Romney Hythe & Dymchurch: This 15-inch line in Kent, built in the 1920s, runs locomotives at about one-third scale and carries real passengers.
Track gauge: the distance between the ra.Ffestiniog Railway: Built in the 1830s to haul slate down from the Welsh mountains, it is among the world's oldest narrow-gauge railways and now carries tourists.
Track gauge: the distance between the ra.Durango & Silverton line: A steam-hauled line in Colorado, opened in 1882 to haul silver ore, and still winding tourists through the San Juan Mountains.
Track gauge: the distance between the ra.Swiss Rhaetian Railway: Metre-gauge track suits steep Alpine terrain; its Albula and Bernina lines are UNESCO-listed and include spiralling viaducts.
Track gauge: the distance between the ra.Japan's older JR lines: Called Cape gauge, it is also used in South Africa and Queensland; narrower track means tighter curves and cheaper mountain building.
Track gauge: the distance between the ra.Japan's Shinkansen: This is standard gauge, used by roughly 55 percent of the world's railways; Japan adopted it for the bullet trains in 1964.
Track gauge: the distance between the ra.Trans-Siberian Railway: Russian gauge is wider than standard, so trains crossing into China must have their wheel sets changed or adjusted at the border.
Track gauge: the distance between the ra.Irish mainline railways: Ireland's gauge is also found in parts of Australia and Brazil, a legacy of 19th-century compromises between rival railway companies.
Track gauge: the distance between the ra.Indian Railways broad gauge: This network carries around 20 million passengers every day, making it one of the busiest rail systems on Earth.
Track gauge: the distance between the ra.Brunel's Great Western: Isambard Kingdom Brunel picked this seven-foot gauge for speed and stability, but Britain standardised on narrower track and the line converted by 1892.

When these famous hoaxes fooled the worl.The Great Moon Hoax: The New York Sun claimed in 1835 that astronomer John Herschel had seen bat-winged people on the Moon, while he was in South Africa unaware.
When these famous hoaxes fooled the worl.The Feejee Mermaid: P. T. Barnum exhibited a monkey torso sewn to a fish tail, billed as a real mermaid.
When these famous hoaxes fooled the worl.The Cardiff Giant: George Hull had a gypsum petrified man buried in New York and then discovered, and Barnum made a copy.
When these famous hoaxes fooled the worl.Piltdown Man: A fake skull, billed as a missing link, fooled scientists for about 40 years until it was exposed in 1953.
When these famous hoaxes fooled the worl.The Cottingley Fairies: Two girls took photos with paper cutouts, and Arthur Conan Doyle was convinced; they admitted the fake in the 1980s.
When these famous hoaxes fooled the worl.Loch Ness Surgeon's Photo: The famous photo of Nessie's neck was a toy submarine with a sculpted head, revealed in 1994.
When these famous hoaxes fooled the worl.BBC's spaghetti harvest: The BBC's Panorama April Fools report in 1957 showed Swiss families picking spaghetti from trees.
When these famous hoaxes fooled the worl.The Hitler Diaries: German magazine Stern paid millions of marks for forged diaries by Konrad Kujau.
When these famous hoaxes fooled the worl.Alien Autopsy film: Ray Santilli's black-and-white film showed an alien; he admitted in 2006 it was a reconstruction.
When these famous hoaxes fooled the worl.Balloon Boy: A Colorado family claimed their son floated away in a helium balloon; he was hiding in the attic.

Champagne bottle sizes.Piccolo (split): Meaning small in Italian, it holds a quarter of a standard bottle and is often served on airlines.
Champagne bottle sizes.Demi: A half bottle is thought to age faster than a standard one, because more of the wine touches the cork's air gap.
Champagne bottle sizes.Standard bottle: Champagne bottle pressure is about six atmospheres, about three times a car tyre, so the cork can fly at around 40 mph.
Champagne bottle sizes.Magnum: It holds two bottles, and many connoisseurs believe champagne ages best in a magnum, thanks to its ratio of wine to air.
Champagne bottle sizes.Jeroboam: Named for a biblical king of Israel, it holds four standard bottles of champagne.
Champagne bottle sizes.Rehoboam: Named for the biblical king who was the son of Solomon, it holds six standard bottles.
Champagne bottle sizes.Methuselah: Named for the oldest man in the Bible, who lived 969 years, it holds eight standard bottles.
Champagne bottle sizes.Salmanazar: Named for an Assyrian king, it holds twelve standard bottles, and the bottle is usually shared at celebrations.
Champagne bottle sizes.Balthazar: Named for one of the three Magi, it holds sixteen standard bottles and weighs about as much as a toddler.
Champagne bottle sizes.Nebuchadnezzar: Named for the Babylonian king, it holds twenty standard bottles and is so heavy it needs two people to pour.

Asian rivers by length.Jordan: The Jordan River is short but hugely significant, and it flows into the Dead Sea, the lowest point on land.
Asian rivers by length.Chao Phraya: The Chao Phraya flows through Bangkok, and it is Thailand's main waterway, nicknamed the River of Kings.
Asian rivers by length.Tigris: The Tigris runs through Baghdad, and it and the Euphrates define Mesopotamia, meaning the land between rivers.
Asian rivers by length.Irrawaddy: The Irrawaddy is Myanmar's lifeline, and it flows from the north to the sea, where it forms a huge delta.
Asian rivers by length.Ganges: The Ganges is sacred to Hindus, and millions bathe in it during festivals such as the Kumbh Mela.
Asian rivers by length.Euphrates: The Euphrates is one of the longest rivers in western Asia, and its waters were crucial to early civilizations like Babylon.
Asian rivers by length.Indus: The Indus gave its name to India, and its valley hosted one of the world's earliest urban civilizations.
Asian rivers by length.Mekong: The Mekong flows through six countries, and it is home to the giant catfish, one of the largest freshwater fish.
Asian rivers by length.Yellow River: The Yellow River is called the cradle of Chinese civilization, and it gets its color from the silt it carries.
Asian rivers by length.Yangtze: The Yangtze is the longest river in Asia, and it is spanned by the Three Gorges Dam, the largest power station in the world.

When these empires were founded.Egypt's New Kingdom: Pharaoh Ahmose I's expulsion of the Hyksos began a golden age that brought us Hatshepsut, Thutmose III and Ramesses II.
When these empires were founded.Achaemenid Persia: Cyrus the Great founded it by conquering Media, Lydia and Babylon, and the Cyrus Cylinder is often called an early charter of human rights.
When these empires were founded.Maurya Empire: Chandragupta Maurya built it, and later his grandson Ashoka ruled most of the subcontinent before turning to Buddhism.
When these empires were founded.Roman Empire: Augustus, once Octavian, became the first emperor; the month of August is named for him.
When these empires were founded.Sasanian Empire: Its founder, Ardashir I, overthrew the Parthians and revived Persian traditions, and the dynasty went on to rival Rome and Byzantium for centuries.
When these empires were founded.Umayyad Caliphate: Following the first four caliphs, this dynasty ruled from Damascus, and its empire stretched from Spain to the borders of India.
When these empires were founded.Charlemagne's empire: The Pope crowned Charlemagne emperor on Christmas Day, creating an early foundation for what later became known as the Holy Roman Empire.
When these empires were founded.Mongol Empire: Temujin took the title Genghis Khan in 1206 and built the largest contiguous land empire in history.
When these empires were founded.Ottoman Empire: Named for its founder Osman I, it lasted over 600 years and ended only in 1922, after capturing Constantinople in 1453.
When these empires were founded.Inca Empire: Inca's rulers built Machu Picchu and a road network of some 40,000 km, and kept records by knotted cords called quipu, since they had no writing.

Provocative modern artworks, by year.Malevich's Black Square: The 1915 painting, a black square on white, was shown high in a corner like a Russian icon, and the artist called it the zero of form.
Provocative modern artworks, by year.Duchamp's Fountain (urinal): Marcel Duchamp signed a store-bought urinal 'R. Mutt', and sparked debate about what counts as art; the original was lost, and replicas were made.
Provocative modern artworks, by year.Warhol's Campbell's Soup Cans: Andy Warhol painted 32 canvases, one for each flavor sold then, and they were first shown in a Los Angeles gallery.
Provocative modern artworks, by year.Spiral Jetty: Robert Smithson's Spiral Jetty is a coil of basalt rock 460 m long in Utah's Great Salt Lake, and its water level has hidden and revealed it.
Provocative modern artworks, by year.Hirst's shark in formaldehyde: Damien Hirst's tiger shark floating in a tank was sold for millions, and the preserved animal was later replaced after it decayed.
Provocative modern artworks, by year.Tracey Emin's My Bed: Tracey Emin's unmade bed, complete with stained sheets and debris, was shortlisted for the Turner Prize and sold at auction in 2014 for about 2.5 million pounds.
Provocative modern artworks, by year.Christo's The Gates: Christo and Jeanne-Claude hung 7,503 saffron-colored fabric panels along Central Park's paths for 16 days in February 2005.
Provocative modern artworks, by year.Hirst's diamond skull: Hirst's platinum cast of a real 18th-century skull, set with 8,601 diamonds, was priced at 50 million pounds, and its forehead holds a huge pear-shaped stone.
Provocative modern artworks, by year.Banksy's shredded painting: Banksy's Girl with Balloon half-shredded itself right after selling at Sotheby's for over a million pounds, and it was later renamed Love is in the Bin.
Provocative modern artworks, by year.The banana taped to a wall: Maurizio Cattelan's Comedian was a fresh banana taped to a wall, which sold for 120,000 dollars at Art Basel Miami, and a visitor later ate one.

Hours of daylight on the June solstice.Ushuaia: The southernmost city in the world sits near Tierra del Fuego and Cape Horn, so its June days are short, with the sun rising late in winter.
Hours of daylight on the June solstice.Sydney: June is midwinter in Sydney, and its short days are brightened by the Vivid light festival, which lights up the Opera House each year in winter.
Hours of daylight on the June solstice.Singapore: On the equator-hugging island, daylight barely changes through the year, because it sits just 1 degree north of the equator.
Hours of daylight on the June solstice.Mumbai: Mumbai has a monsoon season which starts in June, and the long days are often hidden behind thick clouds.
Hours of daylight on the June solstice.Cairo: Cairo, a city on the Nile, sits at about 30 degrees north, so its midsummer day is just over 14 hours.
Hours of daylight on the June solstice.New York: New York sits at about 41 degrees north, and on the summer solstice the sun sets after 8:30 pm, meaning that evenings stay light.
Hours of daylight on the June solstice.London: At the solstice, London's daylight lasts about 16 and a half hours, and its twilight barely ends before dawn returns.
Hours of daylight on the June solstice.Helsinki: Finland's capital lies at 60 degrees north, and in June it has nearly 19 hours of daylight and white nights where it never gets truly dark.
Hours of daylight on the June solstice.Reykjavík: Iceland's capital is just below the Arctic Circle and the sun dips only briefly, so the night sky stays bright all around the solstice.
Hours of daylight on the June solstice.Longyearbyen, Svalbard: The Norwegian archipelago, at 78 degrees north, has the midnight sun from mid-April to late August, when the sun never sets.

Landmark medical texts and journals.Ebers Papyrus: The Ebers Papyrus, a roll over 20 meters long, includes remedies, magic spells and a description of the heart's vessels, and it was bought in Luxor in 1873.
Landmark medical texts and journals.Hippocratic Corpus: Though attributed to Hippocrates, this collection of about 60 works was written by many hands, and it contains the idea of 'first, do no harm'.
Landmark medical texts and journals.Vesalius's Fabrica: Vesalius's De humani corporis fabrica, with beautiful illustrations, corrected Galen's errors by relying on human dissection.
Landmark medical texts and journals.Harvey's De Motu Cordis: William Harvey's slim book on the heart's movement showed that blood circulates around the body, pumped by the heart.
The New England Journal of Medicine is one of the oldest continuously published medical journals, appearing since 1812 under various titles.
Landmark medical texts and journals.The Lancet: The Lancet was founded by surgeon Thomas Wakley, who named it after a sharp surgical instrument to signal his wish to cut through corruption.
Landmark medical texts and journals.Gray's Anatomy: Henry Gray's famous anatomy textbook, illustrated by Henry Vandyke Carter, was based on dissections and has stayed in print for over 160 years.
Landmark medical texts and journals.Index Medicus: Index Medicus, started by John Shaw Billings, gave doctors a way to look up articles by subject long before computers did.
Landmark medical texts and journals.JAMA: JAMA, the Journal of the American Medical Association, began in the year the AMA's organizational struggles were heating up, and publishes weekly.
Landmark medical texts and journals.The Merck Manual: The Merck Manual started as a small pocket reference for doctors and pharmacists, and has grown into a huge medical resource.

Notable Atlantic hurricanes, in order.Galveston hurricane: It is the deadliest natural disaster in US history, killing at least 6,000, after which Galveston built a seawall and raised its streets.
Notable Atlantic hurricanes, in order.Okeechobee hurricane: Lake Okeechobee overflowed, killing about 2,500 people, mostly in Florida.
Notable Atlantic hurricanes, in order.Labor Day hurricane: It remains the most intense hurricane to make landfall in the US, by pressure.
Notable Atlantic hurricanes, in order.Hurricane Camille: It brought a storm surge of about 24 feet, a record at the time.
Notable Atlantic hurricanes, in order.Hurricane Hugo: It hit the Charleston area of South Carolina and caused billions in damage.
Notable Atlantic hurricanes, in order.Hurricane Andrew: It flattened parts of south Florida and led to stronger building codes.
Notable Atlantic hurricanes, in order.Hurricane Mitch: It killed over 11,000 people, mostly in Honduras and Nicaragua.
Notable Atlantic hurricanes, in order.Hurricane Katrina: Levee failures flooded about 80 percent of New Orleans.
Notable Atlantic hurricanes, in order.Hurricane Sandy: Nicknamed Superstorm Sandy, it flooded New York City's subway tunnels.
Notable Atlantic hurricanes, in order.Hurricane Maria: It knocked out power in Puerto Rico for months and was linked to about 3,000 deaths.

The Mongol era, in order.Temüjin named Genghis Khan: Born Temüjin around 1162, he took the title Genghis Khan, roughly 'universal ruler', at a great assembly of the steppe tribes.
The Mongol era, in order.Invasion of Khwarazm: Genghis attacked after the shah had Mongol envoys and merchants killed; the campaign devastated Samarkand, Bukhara and Merv.
The Mongol era, in order.Ögedei becomes Great Khan: Genghis's third son, elected after a two-year regency, founded the capital Karakorum and expanded the Yam relay-post network.
The Mongol era, in order.Mongols sack Kyiv: Batu Khan's army took Kyiv in December 1240 after a siege; the Rus' lands then paid tribute to the Golden Horde for generations.
The Mongol era, in order.Mongols sack Baghdad: Hulagu's siege ended the Abbasid Caliphate; the caliph was killed, and tradition says the Tigris ran black with ink from ruined books.
The Mongol era, in order.Kublai proclaims Yuan dynasty: Kublai took the Chinese dynastic name Yuan, 'origin', from the I Ching, and ruled from Khanbaliq, the site of today's Beijing.
The Mongol era, in order.Second invasion of Japan: A typhoon wrecked Kublai's vast fleet; the Japanese called it kamikaze, 'divine wind', and Mongol attempts on Japan ended for good.
The Mongol era, in order.Yuan dynasty falls: Red Turban rebels under Zhu Yuanzhang pushed the Mongols back to the steppe, and he went on to found the Ming dynasty.
The Mongol era, in order.Battle of Kulikovo: Moscow's Prince Dmitry beat a Golden Horde army on the Don; it didn't end Mongol rule, but it won him the name Donskoy and raised Moscow's standing.
The Mongol era, in order.Timur sacks Delhi: Timur, who claimed Genghis's legacy, plundered Delhi in a massacre from which the weakened Delhi Sultanate never really recovered.

Humanity's toolkit: when each first appe.Stone tools: Found at Lomekwi in Kenya, these tools are older than the genus Homo, so someone other than our ancestors may have made them.
Humanity's toolkit: when each first appe.Controlled fire: Evidence from Wonderwerk Cave in South Africa dates to about a million years ago, and cooking likely helped brains grow.
Humanity's toolkit: when each first appe.Farming: It began in the Fertile Crescent with wheat and barley, and it changed settlements.
Humanity's toolkit: when each first appe.The wheel: The earliest wheels were used for pottery, and wheeled vehicles came later in Mesopotamia.
Humanity's toolkit: when each first appe.Iron smelting: Iron is far more abundant than tin and copper, so iron tools made metal accessible to many.
Humanity's toolkit: when each first appe.Paper: Court official Cai Lun is credited with presenting paper made from bark and rags to the Chinese emperor.
Humanity's toolkit: when each first appe.Printing press: Gutenberg's movable-type press in Mainz printed the Gutenberg Bible around 1455.
Humanity's toolkit: when each first appe.Steam engine (Newcomen): Used to pump water from coal mines, it burned lots of fuel until James Watt improved it.
Humanity's toolkit: when each first appe.Edison's light bulb: Edison's bulb lasted about 13 hours at first; Joseph Swan in Britain made similar bulbs, leading to a joint company.
Humanity's toolkit: when each first appe.The internet (TCP/IP): ARPANET switched to TCP/IP on 1 January 1983, a date sometimes called the internet's birthday.

Little everyday inventions, oldest to ne.Paper drinking straw: Marvin Stone wrapped paper around a pencil because rye-grass straws left grit in his drink.
Little everyday inventions, oldest to ne.Crown bottle cap: William Painter of Baltimore invented it, with 21 teeth that crimp tightly around the bottle's lip.
Little everyday inventions, oldest to ne.Tea bag: According to popular account, Thomas Sullivan sent tea samples in small silk bags and customers dunked the bags directly into the pot.
Little everyday inventions, oldest to ne.Cat's eye road reflector: Inventor Percy Shaw said he was inspired by the reflection of a cat's eyes in his headlights one night in Halifax, England.
Little everyday inventions, oldest to ne.Shopping cart: Sylvan Goldman invented it for an Oklahoma City supermarket, and shoppers at first refused to use it.
Little everyday inventions, oldest to ne.Aerosol spray can: Developed by US Agriculture Department researchers, it was first used in the 1940s to spray insecticides against malaria-carrying mosquitoes.
Little everyday inventions, oldest to ne.Ring-pull drink can: Ermal Fraze invented the pull tab so drinkers needed no opener; discarded rings later became litter, leading to stay-on tabs.
Little everyday inventions, oldest to ne.Ziploc bag: Dow Chemical introduced it in 1968, using a zipper-style seal that originated in earlier work by a Danish inventor.
Little everyday inventions, oldest to ne.Wheeled suitcase: Bernard Sadow patented it, and it took years to catch on because men were reluctant to be seen pulling luggage.
Little everyday inventions, oldest to ne.Bic disposable lighter: Cheap enough to throw away, it helped end the era of refillable pocket lighters.

Famous math constants by value.Euler–Mascheroni constant γ: Its decimal expansion seems endless, and mathematicians still don't know whether this constant is rational or irrational.
Famous math constants by value.Natural log of 2: The alternating harmonic series 1 minus 1/2 plus 1/3 and so on adds up to this number.
Famous math constants by value.Apéry's constant: Roger Apery proved in 1978 that the sum of the reciprocal cubes is irrational.
Famous math constants by value.Square root of 2: Legend says Pythagoreans were shocked to find it can't be written as a fraction.
Famous math constants by value.Golden ratio φ: Ratios of consecutive Fibonacci numbers approach it more and more closely.
Famous math constants by value.Square root of 3: It is the height of an equilateral triangle with side 2.
Famous math constants by value.e: Jacob Bernoulli found it while studying compound interest, and it appears wherever things grow continuously.
Famous math constants by value.π: Pi Day falls on March 14, and computers have now calculated over 100 trillion digits.
Famous math constants by value.Feigenbaum constant δ: It appears in chaos theory whenever systems double their period on the way to chaos, in very different settings.
Famous math constants by value.Tau (two pi): Its advocates say it makes circle formulas more natural, and celebrate Tau Day on June 28.

Charles Darwin's life, in order.Born in Shrewsbury: He was born at The Mount, the son of a wealthy doctor and a Wedgwood pottery heiress, and the grandson of the polymath Erasmus Darwin.
Charles Darwin's life, in order.Studies medicine in Edinburgh: Watching surgery done without anaesthetic horrified him, and he left medicine after two years, turning to natural history instead.
Charles Darwin's life, in order.Sails on HMS Beagle: Darwin was 22 when he sailed; the five-year voyage around the world was meant to chart coasts, and he joined as a gentleman companion for Captain FitzRoy.
Charles Darwin's life, in order.Visits the Galápagos: He noticed the mockingbirds differed by island before the finches, and he had not even labeled his finches by island, so the finch legend is partly myth.
Charles Darwin's life, in order.Marries Emma Wedgwood: Emma was his first cousin, and they had ten children, three of whom died young, which worried him about inherited weakness.
Charles Darwin's life, in order.Moves to Down House: He settled in this Kent village, wrote his great books in its study, and paced a gravel path called the Sandwalk to think.
Charles Darwin's life, in order.Gets Wallace's letter: Alfred Russel Wallace's essay from the Malay islands described natural selection and pushed Darwin to present jointly and finish his own book.
Charles Darwin's life, in order.Publishes Origin of Species: The first print run of about 1,250 copies reportedly sold out on the first day, though the book said almost nothing about human origins.
Charles Darwin's life, in order.Publishes Descent of Man: Here Darwin argued that humans evolved like other species, and developed sexual selection to explain traits like the peacock's tail.
Charles Darwin's life, in order.Dies: He died at 73 and was buried in Westminster Abbey, near Isaac Newton, a rare honor for a man who had upset the church.

Savanna animals by weight.Dung beetle: Some dung beetles navigate by the Milky Way, the only animal known to do so, to roll their ball in a straight line.
Savanna animals by weight.Meerkat: Sentries stand on lookout for hawks and snakes while the group forages, and they use distinct alarm calls for each threat.
Savanna animals by weight.Black-backed jackal: Pairs mate for life, and older offspring help raise younger pups, babysitting and feeding them.
Savanna animals by weight.Cheetah: It cannot roar, and chases last less than a minute, but over short bursts it can reach about 100 km/h.
Savanna animals by weight.Ostrich: Its eye is bigger than its brain, and it is the largest and fastest-running bird, able to sprint about 70 km/h.
Savanna animals by weight.Lion: The only cat that lives in social groups, a lion pride relies on the females for most of the hunting.
Savanna animals by weight.Plains zebra: Each zebra's stripe pattern is unique, and stripes may help deter biting flies.
Savanna animals by weight.Cape buffalo: Nicknamed black death, it is regarded as one of Africa's most dangerous game animals, and herds have driven off lions.
Savanna animals by weight.Hippo: It secretes a reddish oily fluid sometimes called blood sweat that acts as sunscreen and antiseptic, and it is among Africa's deadliest big animals.
Savanna animals by weight.African bush elephant: The largest living land animal, its ears radiate body heat, and its trunk has tens of thousands of muscle bundles.

Classic processors by release year.Intel 4004: The first commercial microprocessor, it had about 2,300 transistors and was designed for a Japanese calculator.
Classic processors by release year.MOS 6502: It was cheap, and it powered the Apple II, Commodore PET and a version in the NES.
Classic processors by release year.Zilog Z80: Made by Zilog, founded by ex-Intel engineers, it powered the ZX Spectrum and many CP/M computers.
Classic processors by release year.Motorola 68000: It powered the original Macintosh, Amiga, Atari ST and the Sega Genesis.
Classic processors by release year.Intel 386: Intel's first 32-bit x86 chip laid the foundation for the PC architecture.
Classic processors by release year.Intel Pentium: A floating-point bug found in 1994 forced a recall costing Intel hundreds of millions of dollars.
Classic processors by release year.AMD Athlon: AMD's chip was the first x86 processor to hit 1 GHz, in March 2000.
Classic processors by release year.Intel Core 2 Duo: Intel moved away from chasing clock speed toward efficiency with this chip, after the Pentium 4.
Classic processors by release year.Intel Core i7: The 'Core i7' name started with Nehalem chips; it has had many generations since.
Classic processors by release year.Apple M1: Apple's first Arm-based chip for Mac used 'unified memory', shared by the CPU and graphics.

When these K-pop acts debuted.Seo Taiji and Boys: The trio were pioneers of K-pop, and they blended hip hop with Korean pop and fused local music with western sounds.
This boy band was the first K-pop idol group, and their name stands for High-five of Teenagers.
When these K-pop acts debuted.BoA: The singer debuted at 13 and helped K-pop break into Japan, and she was among the first K-pop stars there.
When these K-pop acts debuted.TVXQ: This five-member boy band was big in Asia, and it was formed by SM Entertainment, and the group's name means 'rising gods'.
When these K-pop acts debuted.Super Junior: The group became known for having many members, and its 'rotating' lineup, and its members have been part of subunits.
When these K-pop acts debuted.Girls' Generation: The nine-member girl group's song 'Gee' was a mega-hit, and it helped define the girl group era.
When these K-pop acts debuted.BTS: The seven-member group became the first Korean act to top the Billboard Hot 100, and it started from a small company.
When these K-pop acts debuted.Twice: The nine-member girl group was formed on the TV show Sixteen, and it is known for catchy hits like 'Cheer Up'.
When these K-pop acts debuted.Blackpink: The four-member group was the first K-pop girl group to play Coachella, and they have the most-subscribed music channel on YouTube.
When these K-pop acts debuted.NewJeans: The group debuted with a single, and it became a fast hit, and the members are known for Y2K-inspired pop.

Atomic number of the element in each.Party balloon gas: Helium is so light it escapes Earth's atmosphere, and we get it from natural gas deposits.
Atomic number of the element in each.Pencil 'lead' (graphite): No lead at all: graphite is carbon layers that slide off onto paper, a name left over from lead styluses.
Atomic number of the element in each.Glowing red signs: Neon gives that red-orange glow, and other colors come from other gases or phosphor coatings.
Atomic number of the element in each.Soda can metal: Aluminium was once costlier than gold, and Napoleon III reportedly served his top guests with aluminium cutlery.
Atomic number of the element in each.Computer chips: The second most abundant element in Earth's crust, it is found in ordinary sand as silica.
Atomic number of the element in each.The mineral in bones: About 99% of the body's calcium sits in bones and teeth.
Atomic number of the element in each.Electrical wiring metal: Its conductivity and ease of drawing into wire made it the electrical standard, and Cyprus gives it its name.
Atomic number of the element in each.Pirate treasure doubloons: Real pirates rarely buried treasure, and doubloons were Spanish gold coins.
Atomic number of the element in each.Old fever thermometers: The only metal liquid at room temperature, it is toxic, which is why glass thermometers were phased out.
Atomic number of the element in each.Nuclear power plant fuel: A fingertip-sized uranium fuel pellet holds about as much energy as a ton of coal.

Mobile operating systems by debut.Palm OS: Palm's handheld system came with Graffiti, a handwriting alphabet that taught millions of people to write letters in a single stroke.
Mobile operating systems by debut.BlackBerry OS: Famous for push email and tiny physical keyboards, it made the BlackBerry the status phone of business users and politicians.
Mobile operating systems by debut.Pocket PC: Microsoft's name for its handheld platform, built on Windows CE, which paved the way for the later Windows Mobile line.
Mobile operating systems by debut.iOS: It was originally called iPhone OS, and was renamed iOS in 2010 when it spread to the iPad and iPod touch.
Mobile operating systems by debut.Android: It began as a camera software startup in 2003, was bought by Google in 2005, and first shipped on the HTC Dream in 2008.
Mobile operating systems by debut.webOS: Born on the Palm Pre, it later went to HP and then LG, and today it still runs inside many LG smart TVs.
Mobile operating systems by debut.Windows Phone: Microsoft's tile-based Metro design replaced Windows Mobile, but the platform never won enough apps and was eventually retired.
Mobile operating systems by debut.Firefox OS: Mozilla's web-based phone system was aimed at cheap handsets in developing markets, and it ended on phones around 2016.
Mobile operating systems by debut.KaiOS: A descendant of Firefox OS, it powers inexpensive feature phones and brought apps like WhatsApp to buttons-and-screen handsets.
Mobile operating systems by debut.HarmonyOS: Huawei built it after US trade restrictions cut its access to Google services, and it spread beyond phones to watches and TVs.

UK and Channel Islands towns, north to s.Lerwick, Shetland: Lerwick hosts Up Helly Aa each winter, when locals in Viking dress parade with torches and burn a longship.
UK and Channel Islands towns, north to s.Kirkwall, Orkney: St Magnus Cathedral, begun in 1137 in red and yellow sandstone, dominates the town and is nicknamed the Light in the North.
UK and Channel Islands towns, north to s.Inverness: The gateway to the Highlands and Loch Ness, it sits on the Moray Firth, and Culloden battlefield is nearby.
UK and Channel Islands towns, north to s.Edinburgh: Arthur's Seat, an extinct volcano, rises right beside the city centre, and the city is split into Old Town and New Town.
UK and Channel Islands towns, north to s.Belfast: The Titanic was built in its shipyard, and the city has a museum on the ship beside the slipway.
UK and Channel Islands towns, north to s.Manchester: The world's first stored-program computer, nicknamed Baby, ran here in 1948.
UK and Channel Islands towns, north to s.Birmingham: The city is often said to have more canals than Venice, and its canal network helped build the industrial revolution.
UK and Channel Islands towns, north to s.London: The Prime Meridian runs through Greenwich, in the east of the city, and defines longitude zero.
UK and Channel Islands towns, north to s.Plymouth: The Pilgrim Fathers sailed from here in the Mayflower in 1620, and Francis Drake famously played bowls on the Hoe.
UK and Channel Islands towns, north to s.St Helier, Jersey: Jersey is a Crown Dependency, not part of the UK, with its own government, laws and stamps.

Famous psychology experiments, by year.Thorndike's puzzle-box cats: Edward Thorndike timed cats escaping puzzle boxes and described the Law of Effect: behavior that is rewarded is repeated.
Famous psychology experiments, by year.Little Albert: John Watson and Rosalie Rayner conditioned a baby to fear a white rat; it would be considered unethical today.
Famous psychology experiments, by year.Asch conformity lines: Solomon Asch found that about a third of answers matched a group's obviously wrong claims about line lengths.
Famous psychology experiments, by year.Harlow's monkeys: Harlow's baby monkeys preferred a soft cloth surrogate mother to a wire one that gave milk, showing the importance of comfort.
Famous psychology experiments, by year.Milgram obedience study: Milgram found that around two-thirds of volunteers delivered what they thought was a maximum shock when told to continue.
Famous psychology experiments, by year.Darley and Latané bystanders: The bystander effect, that more witnesses can mean less help, was studied after the 1964 murder of Kitty Genovese.
Famous psychology experiments, by year.Stanford Prison Experiment: Philip Zimbardo's study, planned for two weeks, was halted after six days, and its validity is now widely criticized.
Famous psychology experiments, by year.Rosenhan's fake patients: Eight healthy people got themselves admitted to psychiatric hospitals by saying they heard voices, and then stayed for weeks.
Famous psychology experiments, by year.Loftus car-crash memory: Elizabeth Loftus showed that changing one word, smashed rather than hit, changed how fast people remembered cars going.
Famous psychology experiments, by year.Tversky and Kahneman's Linda: In the Linda problem, people judge bank teller and feminist as likelier than bank teller, a logical error called the conjunction fallacy.

Milestones in weather and climate scienc.Howard names the clouds: Luke Howard, an amateur meteorologist, gave clouds Latin names such as cumulus, stratus and cirrus, still used today.
Milestones in weather and climate scienc.Fourier's greenhouse effect: Joseph Fourier realized Earth would be far colder without its atmosphere, an early step toward the greenhouse effect.
Milestones in weather and climate scienc.Tyndall: CO2 traps heat: John Tyndall measured in the lab that gases like carbon dioxide and water vapor absorb heat, unlike oxygen and nitrogen.
Milestones in weather and climate scienc.FitzRoy's first forecasts: Captain of Darwin's Beagle, Robert FitzRoy coined the word forecast and published the first daily weather forecasts in The Times.
Milestones in weather and climate scienc.Arrhenius predicts warming: Svante Arrhenius calculated that doubling carbon dioxide would warm the planet by several degrees, and thought that might be welcome.
Milestones in weather and climate scienc.US hurricanes get names: The US weather service began giving hurricanes women's names in 1953, and added men's names in 1979.
Milestones in weather and climate scienc.First weather satellite: TIROS-1 sent back the first television pictures of Earth's cloud cover from space in April 1960.
Milestones in weather and climate scienc.Lorenz's butterfly effect: Edward Lorenz found that tiny changes in a weather model can cause huge differences, giving us the butterfly effect and chaos theory.
Milestones in weather and climate scienc.Ozone hole discovered: British Antarctic Survey scientists published the finding of the ozone hole in 1985, and the Montreal Protocol followed in 1987.
Milestones in weather and climate scienc.First IPCC report: The Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change, created in 1988, issued its first assessment in 1990, warning of warming from emissions.

How far away is it from Earth's surface?.The ISS: It circles Earth about every 90 minutes, so astronauts see around 16 sunrises a day.
How far away is it from Earth's surface?.Hubble Space Telescope: It was repaired in orbit by shuttle astronauts after its mirror flaw was discovered in 1990.
How far away is it from Earth's surface?.GPS satellites: These satellites circle twice a day and carry atomic clocks, which need corrections for relativity.
How far away is it from Earth's surface?.Geostationary satellites: A satellite at this altitude orbits once a day, hanging over one spot. Arthur C. Clarke proposed the idea in 1945.
How far away is it from Earth's surface?.The Moon: It drifts away from Earth by about 3.8 centimetres a year.
How far away is it from Earth's surface?.Mars at its closest: Its closest approaches come only about every 26 months, and the distance varies from one to the next.
How far away is it from Earth's surface?.The Sun: Light from it takes about 8 minutes 20 seconds to reach us.
How far away is it from Earth's surface?.Voyager 1: Launched in 1977, it entered interstellar space in 2012. Radio signals take over 22 hours to reach it.
How far away is it from Earth's surface?.Proxima Centauri: The nearest known star beyond the Sun is a dim red dwarf, and it has at least one planet in the habitable zone.
How far away is it from Earth's surface?.Andromeda Galaxy: It is on course to collide with the Milky Way in a few billion years, and it can be seen with the naked eye on dark nights.

Tiny critters, weighed in grams.Fruit fly: Fruit flies are a genetics workhorse, and their short lives let scientists track many generations, which has won several Nobel Prizes.
Tiny critters, weighed in grams.Mosquito: Only females bite, because they need blood protein to make eggs, and males live on nectar.
Tiny critters, weighed in grams.Housefly: A housefly tastes with its feet, landing on food and sampling it as it walks.
Tiny critters, weighed in grams.Honeybee: A honeybee beats its wings about 230 times a second, and workers share the way to flowers with a waggle dance.
Tiny critters, weighed in grams.Monarch butterfly: Monarchs fly up to about 4,000 km to winter in Mexican forests, and no single butterfly makes the whole round trip.
Tiny critters, weighed in grams.Etruscan shrew: The world's smallest mammal by weight has a heart that beats over 1,000 times a minute, and it must eat about its own body weight daily.
Tiny critters, weighed in grams.Ruby-throated hummingbird: Each year it crosses the Gulf of Mexico, a flight of some 800 km, on tiny wings that beat dozens of times a second.
Tiny critters, weighed in grams.Blue tit: Blue tits can see ultraviolet light, which helps them pick mates and spot insects that look plain to us.
Tiny critters, weighed in grams.House sparrow: Spread around the world with human settlement, it lives in towns and farms, though numbers have dropped in many European cities.
Tiny critters, weighed in grams.Syrian hamster: Every pet golden hamster descends from a family caught in Syria in 1930, and cheek pouches can stretch to carry food.

Early Islamic history, in order.The Hijra: The Prophet Muhammad's migration from Mecca to Medina marks year one of the Islamic calendar.
Early Islamic history, in order.Umayyads take power: The dynasty made Damascus its capital, and ruled a vast empire stretching from Spain to Central Asia.
Early Islamic history, in order.Dome of the Rock completed: Built in Jerusalem, it is one of the earliest great works of Islamic architecture, and its golden dome was added later.
Early Islamic history, in order.Conquest of Iberia begins: The general Tariq ibn Ziyad crossed to Spain, and Gibraltar's name comes from Jabal Tariq, the mountain of Tariq.
Early Islamic history, in order.Abbasid revolution: The new dynasty shifted the center of the empire east to Iraq, and soon founded Baghdad as its capital.
Early Islamic history, in order.House of Wisdom flourishes: Scholars in Baghdad translated Greek, Persian and Indian works here, and al-Khwarizmi's name gave us the word algorithm.
Early Islamic history, in order.Fatimids found Cairo: Its name means "the Victorious", and the Fatimids also founded the al-Azhar mosque and university.
Early Islamic history, in order.Saladin takes Jerusalem: After defeating the Crusaders at Hattin, the Kurdish leader was admired even by his enemies, including Richard the Lionheart.
Early Islamic history, in order.Mongols sack Baghdad: Hulagu's army destroyed the Abbasid capital, and the Tigris is said to have run black with ink from the books thrown in.
Early Islamic history, in order.Granada falls: The fall of the last Muslim kingdom in Spain came the same year Columbus sailed, and the Alhambra remains from it.

Notorious hacks and breaches.Kevin Mitnick arrested: The famed hacker was caught after a long chase by the FBI, and later became a security consultant.
Notorious hacks and breaches.Conficker worm: The worm infected millions of computers, and Microsoft offered a $250,000 reward for its creators.
Notorious hacks and breaches.PlayStation Network hack: The PlayStation Network was offline for around three weeks, with details on some 77 million accounts exposed.
Notorious hacks and breaches.Target data breach: Attackers entered via credentials stolen from a heating and cooling contractor, and took about 40 million card numbers.
Notorious hacks and breaches.Sony Pictures hack: The US blamed North Korea, and the attack came as the studio released a comedy about assassinating Kim Jong Un.
Notorious hacks and breaches.Ashley Madison leak: Hackers leaked data from the affair-dating site, exposing tens of millions of users and causing lawsuits.
Notorious hacks and breaches.Equifax breach: An unpatched web software flaw exposed data on about 147 million people, one of the largest ever leaks.
Notorious hacks and breaches.SolarWinds hack: Attackers slipped malware into a software update used by about 18,000 customers, including US government agencies.
Notorious hacks and breaches.Colonial Pipeline ransomware: A ransomware gang shut down a major US fuel pipeline, causing panic buying at gas stations in several states.
Notorious hacks and breaches.MOVEit breach: A flaw in a file-transfer tool let the Cl0p gang steal data from thousands of organisations worldwide.

Bubbles, crashes and busts.Dutch tulip mania: At the 1637 peak a single rare bulb reportedly cost more than a skilled craftsman earned in a year, though historians debate how widespread the damage was.
Bubbles, crashes and busts.South Sea Bubble: Isaac Newton lost a fortune in it, reportedly remarking that he could calculate the motion of the heavenly bodies but not the madness of people.
Bubbles, crashes and busts.Knickerbocker Trust panic: A run on a New York trust company set off panic that J.P. Morgan helped contain, and which led to the Federal Reserve in 1913.
Bubbles, crashes and busts.Wall Street Crash: Black Tuesday, October 29, helped trigger the Great Depression, and the Dow did not regain its 1929 peak until 1954.
Bubbles, crashes and busts.Black Monday: On October 19 the Dow fell about 22% in one day, still its biggest one-day percentage drop on record.
Bubbles, crashes and busts.Barings Bank collapse: Rogue trader Nick Leeson's hidden losses sank Britain's oldest merchant bank, founded in 1762, which was sold for one pound.
Bubbles, crashes and busts.Dot-com bust: The Nasdaq peaked in March 2000, then lost roughly three quarters of its value over the next two and a half years.
Bubbles, crashes and busts.Enron bankruptcy: The Texas energy giant hid debts in off-books partnerships; its fall destroyed auditor Arthur Andersen and led to the Sarbanes-Oxley law.
Bubbles, crashes and busts.Lehman Brothers collapse: The largest bankruptcy in US history, with over $600 billion in assets, turned a US housing problem into a global financial crisis.
Bubbles, crashes and busts.Silicon Valley Bank fails: It collapsed in about two days after depositors tried to withdraw some $42 billion in a single day, fueled by social media panic.

Exoplanets by length of their year.55 Cancri e: A scorching, rocky super-Earth with lava seas, it is so close to its star that its year is shorter than a day on Earth.
Exoplanets by length of their year.HD 209458 b: The first exoplanet seen crossing in front of its star, and the first to show an atmosphere; its nickname is Osiris.
Exoplanets by length of their year.51 Pegasi b: The first planet found around a Sun-like star, in 1995, earned its finders the 2019 Nobel Prize in Physics.
Exoplanets by length of their year.TRAPPIST-1e: One of seven planets around a tiny star about 40 light-years away, and it lies in the habitable zone.
Exoplanets by length of their year.Proxima Centauri b: It orbits the closest star to the Sun, 4.2 light-years away.
Exoplanets by length of their year.Kepler-186f: It was the first Earth-sized planet found in another star's habitable zone, in 2014.
Exoplanets by length of their year.Kepler-16b: Called a 'Tatooine', it orbits two stars at once.
Exoplanets by length of their year.Kepler-22b: It was the first Kepler planet confirmed in a habitable zone, in 2011, although it is much larger than Earth.
Exoplanets by length of their year.Kepler-452b: Nicknamed 'Earth's cousin', it orbits a Sun-like star about 1,400 light-years away.
Exoplanets by length of their year.Beta Pictoris b: Directly photographed in a young system whose star is only about 20 million years old, circled by a huge debris disc.

Adult animated series premieres.Beavis and Butt-Head: MTV's crude teen duo came from Mike Judge, who later created the gentler King of the Hill.
Adult animated series premieres.King of the Hill: Mike Judge's show about a Texas propane salesman and his family ran 13 seasons on Fox.
Adult animated series premieres.Futurama: Created by Matt Groening, it was cancelled and revived several times. Several writers hold advanced degrees in maths and science.
Adult animated series premieres.Aqua Teen Hunger Force: A 2007 Boston bomb scare was caused by the show's LED ad boards, which police mistook for explosives.
Adult animated series premieres.American Dad!: Seth MacFarlane's show features a CIA agent, Stan Smith. It moved from Fox to TBS in 2014.
Adult animated series premieres.Archer: H. Jon Benjamin voices the suave spy Sterling Archer, and also Bob in Bob's Burgers.
Adult animated series premieres.Bob's Burgers: Linda Belcher is voiced by John Roberts, a man, who also voices Linda's silly side with real affection.
Adult animated series premieres.Rick and Morty: Created by Justin Roiland and Dan Harmon, it caused a 2017 McDonald's Szechuan-sauce frenzy after a catchphrase.
Adult animated series premieres.BoJack Horseman: Netflix's tragicomic show about a washed-up horse star, voiced by Will Arnett, ran six seasons to 2020.
Adult animated series premieres.Big Mouth: Netflix's puberty comedy from Nick Kroll and Andrew Goldberg features Hormone Monsters who steer teenagers' impulses.

Books behind Disney films, by publicatio.The Hunchback of Notre-Dame: Victor Hugo wrote it partly to save the cathedral, and its popularity spurred restoration. The Disney version changes the grim ending.
Books behind Disney films, by publicatio.The Little Mermaid: In Hans Christian Andersen's original, the mermaid does not get the prince and dissolves into sea foam.
Books behind Disney films, by publicatio.Alice in Wonderland: Lewis Carroll was a mathematician named Charles Dodgson. Disney's 1951 film merges two books.
Books behind Disney films, by publicatio.Pinocchio: Carlo Collodi's wooden puppet is far less polite in the original, squashing the talking cricket early on.
Books behind Disney films, by publicatio.The Jungle Book: Rudyard Kipling was born in Bombay. His stories feature Baloo, Bagheera and Mowgli.
Books behind Disney films, by publicatio.Peter and Wendy: J. M. Barrie gave the rights to Peter Pan to the Great Ormond Street Hospital, which still benefits.
Books behind Disney films, by publicatio.Bambi, a Life in the Woods: Felix Salten's Austrian novel was banned in Nazi Germany as political allegory.
Books behind Disney films, by publicatio.Winnie-the-Pooh: A. A. Milne's bear was inspired by a real black bear named Winnie and his son's toy.
Books behind Disney films, by publicatio.Mary Poppins: P. L. Travers disliked Disney's adaptation, though the film won five Oscars.
Books behind Disney films, by publicatio.The Hundred and One Dalmatians: Dodie Smith's novel introduced Cruella de Vil. The 1961 film used xerography to copy spotty puppies cheaply.

When these famous chefs and food writers.Brillat-Savarin: His 1825 book The Physiology of Taste gave us the line 'Tell me what you eat, and I will tell you what you are.'
When these famous chefs and food writers.Marie-Antoine Carême: Called the 'king of chefs', he built towering pastry showpieces and cooked for Talleyrand and a tsar.
When these famous chefs and food writers.Auguste Escoffier: He organized the kitchen brigade system used worldwide and created Peach Melba at London's Savoy.
When these famous chefs and food writers.Julia Child: She worked for the OSS during WWII and brought French cooking to American television in The French Chef.
When these famous chefs and food writers.Paul Bocuse: The Lyon chef held three Michelin stars from 1965 for decades, and gave his name to the Bocuse d'Or.
When these famous chefs and food writers.Alice Waters: Her Berkeley restaurant Chez Panisse, opened in 1971, helped launch the farm-to-table movement.
When these famous chefs and food writers.Anthony Bourdain: His 2000 memoir Kitchen Confidential lifted the lid on restaurant kitchens before his travel show Parts Unknown.
When these famous chefs and food writers.Ferran Adrià: His Catalan restaurant elBulli pioneered foams and molecular cuisine before closing in 2011.
When these famous chefs and food writers.Gordon Ramsay: A knee injury ended his hopes of a football career; he was on the books at Rangers as a teenager.
When these famous chefs and food writers.Jamie Oliver: He rose to fame with The Naked Chef in 1999, and campaigned to reform British school dinners.
